If you have ever struggled to make your house truly feel like a home, you are not alone. That is why every seasonal chapter in Homemaking with Babs includes ideas for adding the comforting, personal touches that make a home feel like yours.

While we were in Charleston, we posted on Stories asking if anyone would let me come over and help organize their home.

Lauren invited us in.

We thought the day would be about sharing a few organizing tips, but what it became was so much more.

Lauren already had a beautiful, organized house. But since losing her mom two years ago shortly after she started building her house, she had been struggling to now make it truly feel like home. She missed having her mom there to say, “Okay, here is what you do.”

So we spent the day making small, comforting changes using ideas from my new book.

We brought her mother’s vase and silver out of storage. We displayed her children’s artwork, created a craft and homework cart for calmer afternoons, and framed old photographs of her mom so Lauren could see her every time she walked through the door.

Nothing we did completely changed her house. But each little detail made it feel warmer, more personal and more connected to the people she loves.

Because homemaking is not about having a perfect house or buying more things. It is about bringing the meaningful things you already have into your everyday life and creating a home where the people inside feel seen, loved and cared for.

Lauren later told me there were so many things she did not know she still needed her mom to teach her.

That is why I wrote Homemaking with Babs. So whenever you need a little motherly guidance, you can open the book and hear me say, “Okay, here is what you do.” ❤️
items.transcript: Here's everything I did to help a woman I had never met make her house feel a little more like a home. This is Lauren. Since losing her mom two years ago, she wished she still had her there to say, Okay, here's what you do. I brought my new book along with a few ideas and we got to work. I brought hydrangeas and showed her my trick for making the flowers last twice as long. Then we placed them in her mother's vase, bringing something her mom loved into the room. We made a fall simmer pot to fill the house with a warm, welcoming scent. Then we hung fresh eucalyptus in the shower. Little comforts like these can make everyday routines feel warmer and more cared for. Her mother's beautiful silver had been tucked away, so we cleaned it with foil, baking soda, lemon, and boiling water. As the tarnish disappeared, her mom's silver could become part of daily life again instead of remaining hidden away. For those smelly things that come with having kids, I put vodka in a spray bottle to freshen sneakers and sports gear. Sometimes it's the small practical things that make a busy home feel a little easier to manage. We talked briefly about the importance of family meetings, giving everyone a chance to share what's going on, solve problems together, and feel heard. We turned a blank wall into a gallery for her children's artwork using washi tape to display each masterpiece without damaging the walls. It gave the children's creativity a place to be seen and made the room feel more personal. We also created a craft and homework cart, giving the children supplies a home and making busy after-school hours feel calmer and more relaxed. Then we went through old family photographs that had been hiding in bins. We framed pictures of her mom and placed them on the entryway table where Lauren could feel like her mom is watching over her. Instead of keeping those memories packed away, her mom could become part of everyday life again. Because making a house feel like home is not about buying more things. It's about bringing the meaningful things you already have into the life you are living now. Later, she told me there were so many things she did not know she still needed her mom to teach her. That's why I wrote Homemaking with Babs. So whenever you need a little motherly guidance, you can open the book and hear me say, Okay, here's what you do.

We celebrated Labor Day a little early this year because I was about to hit the road for the Homemaking with Babs book tour, and I couldn’t leave without squeezing in one last summer dinner at the beach❤️

And what a way to send off summer!

I did as much of the prep as I could at home, packed it all up, and finished dinner right at the beach. If your beach or park has grills available, take advantage of them! It’s such a fun way to turn an ordinary summer evening into something that feels really special. Just be sure to check your beach’s rules before you plan your menu.

Now that I’m home from the first stops of the book tour, I’m finally getting to share everything we made.

And what a menu it was!

Comment “MENU” and I’ll send you the full menu and recipes
items.transcript: Here's everything I made for our early Labor Day celebration before I left for my book tour. I started at home with my mojito watermelon salad. Then I prepped my corn and orzo salad and made the lobster salad for our lobster rolls. I marinated a skirt steak to bring along and for dessert I made an Atlantic beach pie. It's this incredible sweet and tangy lemon and lime pie with a salty cracker crust. Perfect for a summer dinner at the beach. Then everything went into the coolers and out came my handy dandy laundry basket. Once we got to the beach it was time to finish the menu. First I grilled the corn for the orzo salad, toasted the bread for our crab dip, and roasted the jalapenos for a roasted jalapeno guacamole. Then I made the crab dip right on the grill, hot and bubbly with pickled jalapenos on top. So good. And here's the easiest little appetizer, borzón surrounded by bugles for dipping. We learned this combination from our Belgian friend whose aunt used to serve it and we've been making it ever since. With all the appetizers out it was time for the skirt steak. This is such an easy thing to bring to the beach because it cooks in about 3 minutes per side. I sliced it up and spooned homemade chimichurri right over the top. Then I cut that grilled corn off the cob and added it to the orzo salad with fresh arugula and the rest of the dressing and gave it a good toss. Next up, the lobster rolls. I always use brioche buns with a little bibb lettuce then pile in that lobster salad. To finish the mojito watermelon salad I added fresh mint, pistachios, feta, and a delicious mojito dressing. And finally dessert. I topped the Atlantic beach pie with plenty of whipped cream and finished it with fresh lemon and lime zest. One last summer feast.

The very first event of the Homemaking with Babs book tour felt especially meaningful because we held it right here at the Basket House. For the first time ever, we opened the doors and welcomed 60 of my online family inside to tour the home, hear some of its stories, and celebrate the book together.

The Basket House is where so much of Homemaking with Babs was photographed, so beginning the tour here felt like the perfect way to bring everything full circle.

And it reminded me of something I really wanted this book to capture: homemaking is about so much more than cleaning and organizing.

Yes, it is about creating systems that make life easier, staying on top of home maintenance, building routines that work, and having seasonal checklists and practical tips to help you care for your home.

But it is also about what happens inside that home.

It is about gathering around the table, welcoming people in, feeding the people you love, celebrating together, and making your home a place people want to return to.

That is why Homemaking with Babs also includes so much of what I have learned over a lifetime of hosting and entertaining, from how to set a table and the entertaining essentials I always keep on hand, to simple ways to spruce up for the season and even my trick for nearly doubling the size of your table when you need a few more seats.

Because your home is meant to be cared for, but it is also meant to be lived in, gathered in, and shared.

What a special way to begin this book tour and thank you @birchlane for helping make this such a special day! 

Homemaking with Babs is available tomorrow
items.transcript: To celebrate the release of Homemaking with Babs, for the very first time ever, we opened the doors to the basket house. This little home was built in the 1800s and was once a working basket shop where baskets were woven and sold. Today, those baskets still fill the home and remind us of the history held within these walls. The basket house is also where we photograph so much of Homemaking with Babs, so opening the doors and welcoming everyone inside felt like the perfect way to celebrate. Because to me, homemaking has always been about so much more than keeping a house clean. It's about caring for your home, staying organized, and creating simple systems that make everyday life easier. But it's also about opening your doors and welcoming people in. There's an entire section of Homemaking with Babs devoted to hosting with all those things no one really teaches you. How to get your house ready for guests, how to plan and prepare for a party, or how to properly set a table, and even my folding table hack that can double your seating when you need to make room for more. Because good hosting isn't about having the perfect home or throwing the perfect party. It's about being prepared enough that when your guests walk through the door, you can actually enjoy having them there. That's really what Homemaking with Babs is all about. Caring for your home, creating systems that make life easier, and knowing how to welcome the people you love into it. And seeing the basket house filled with all of you felt like bringing those pages to life. Homemaking with Babs is officially yours tomorrow, and I cannot wait for you to bring it into your home.

items.transcript: Here's everything I did and made to help one of my kids move into a new home, and I didn't just bring a housewarming gift. I came ready to roll up my sleeves. Before the furniture arrived, I opened the windows and got to work on all those little jobs that are so much easier to do before move-in day. Of course, I brought along my new book, Homemaking with Babs. You'll see why. I started by making a few of my favorite DIY cleaners. They're simple to make, use ingredients you probably already have at home, and are perfect for tackling all those little jobs around the house. The carpet had a few old stains, so I used my homemade carpet cleaner and gave those spots a little attention. You'd be surprised what you can remove with a few simple ingredients. The showerhead needed some help, so I cleaned away the mineral buildup and got that water flowing again. Another one of my favorite little tricks, write the paint color of the room behind the switch plate. When you need a touch-up, you'll know exactly what color to use. Then I worked my way through the appliances. I pulled out the dishwasher filter and gave it a good cleaning. It's one of those parts of your home that's easy to forget about, but food and buildup collect in there, so it needs a little attention every so often. And that's really the thing. These aren't just tips for moving into a new home. They're things we should all be doing to take care of the homes we live in. Homemaking with Babs walks you through what needs to be done and, just as importantly, when to do it. Next, the garbage disposal. I made my cleaning slushie and gave it a whirl. Surprisingly, ours wasn't too bad, but imagine what could be lurking in yours. Don't forget the drain. That needs to be cleaned every so often too. Once the appliances were taken care of, I put a simmer pot on the stove. There's nothing like a beautiful seasonal scent filling the air to start making a new house feel like home. We even found a few ants. Before you call an exterminator, try this little trick. Borax and sugar with cotton balls. And finally, I gave the washer and dryer a good cleaning too. They're two appliances we depend on all the time, but don't always remember they need a little care themselves. I also like to use charcoal to help absorb unwanted smells and moisture. Place a few charcoal bags in closets, cabinets, the laundry room, or anywhere that could use a little freshening up. After 50 years of homemaking, I put everything I know into Homemaking with Babs, the owner's manual your home should have come with.

items.transcript: At 77, here are the household tricks I wish I knew at 30. Use borax and sugar to get rid of ants. Works better than any $500 exterminator. Use Elmer's glue, baking soda, and contact lens solution to clean all those hard-to-reach areas in your car. Use white wine to get rid of red wine stains. Easy as that. Just blot with cold water and let dry. Use charcoal to control moisture and odor in all parts of your home. items.transcript: Here's everything I did to help my daughter with four kids get her home ready for back to school. Every season gives us a fresh start. That's exactly how I organized my new book, Homemaking with Babs, by the seasons of the year. When transitioning to fall, things get very busy, so that's why it's important to plan ahead. An organized, clean refrig and freezer just makes everything feel lighter. We set up dinner bins for the week, added a few freezer meals, plus wellness cubes whenever someone's not feeling too well. It's all about simple systems that work and make life easier. And yes, we even made a stomach bug bucket, because 2 a.m. is not the time to be searching for supplies. That's real life. We used my five-bin declutter system to tackle the kids' rooms. It keeps you focused and keeps you moving. We also set up a designated area for weekly family meetings, a homework station, and after-school drop zones. And the most important part, everyone gets involved, which is woven throughout my book, because running a home shouldn't fall on just one person. So we practice shoes in the drop zone, lunchbox and water bottle in the sink, backpack hung up, homework where it belongs, chore charts, the laundry loop, even carrying baskets upstairs. Don't be afraid to test your systems with your family, walk through them together, and order Homemaking with Babs today.
